doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Writing for NBC's The Funny Side
summary: He wrote a weekly group production number for Gene Kelly's comedy show, comedic and ephemeral, recording it off the TV at home.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Can you give me an example?
Well the stuff that I wrote for that show?

The show was called “The Funny Side” on NBC. Gene Kelly was the host. A weekly comedy show. And my job was to write a production number each week. It had to last nearly five minutes and it had to involve up to twelve cast members. And the more cast members were involved, the better they liked it. So it was really strange songwriting. It was writing for groups of people, for two people here who would answer what two people over there did, and they would react lyrically according to some plot. Each week the song had to be about the week’s topic. So I had to write songs about the funny side of blah-blah, the funny side of blah-blah. The funny side of money. The funny side of news. The funny side of television. You know, the funny side of advertising. So I had to write songs that were like funny, it was comedy. It was comedy writing.
Did it ever irk you that you were writing things that probably were going to be used once? Or was it just the job?

One of the songs, called “The Sports Page,” I used later on in life, but it was the only one of the songs of the bunch that I wrote that had any application later. Yes, it was, there was something uncomfortable about knowing that you were writing something that was deliberately ephemeral. It was going to be gone. And in those days there wasn’t even routine taping of a show. It was done once.
It’s not going to go into syndication.

I’d love to — I do have recordings that I made myself from when I was there, I’ve listened on television at home to the show and I put a microphone up next to the speaker of the TV and recorded it onto my Tandberg you know. But that’s how long ago it was.
